newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan offers bi-monthly CDs to improve liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Jordan offers bi-monthly CDs to improve liquidity.

text.p: The Central Bank of Jordan said on Wednesday it would now offer banks bi-monthly certificates of deposit instead of weekly to help them manage their liquidity.
The Central Bank's first bi-monthly 30 million dinar auction will be offered on April 26 after the end of the Moslem Eid al-Adha holiday, the bank said.

Central Bank CDs, which have become the key benchmark interest rates, have been offered on a weekly basis since they were first introduced in 1993 as part of efforts to develop the domestic capital market.
Officials said the new system would give banks more time between each offering to assess their requirements.
"It will help stimulate the interbank market and allow banks to better manage and plan their liquidity needs and attain more flexibility," said a Central Bank official.

The official stressed the move was not linked to tight monetary policy, which remained in place, but was intended to develop the interbank market which the Central Bank has been pushing banks to activate.
The Central Bank has been using the weekly CDs issues to absorb liquidity and is its main way to manage interest rates.
The bank also announced its last 15 million dinar weekly auction on Wednesday ahead of a long Eid al-Adha holiday starting April 16.

CD interest yields released on Wednesday from last week's similar 15 million dinars auction for three-month and six month certificates remained unchanged at 9.250 percent and 9.500 percent respectively.
Outstanding CDs stood at around 800 million dinars.
The Central Bank keeps a high interest rate policy to make dinar-denominated assets attractive and prevent a flow of dinars into dollar-denominated assets.
Repurchase agreements as collateral to weekly CDs stood unchanged at 10.000 percent.
